cell.label: Suspected coccidioidomycosis: pneumonia symptoms in patient exposed to endemic areas. Order serology. Result?
If the patient is pregnant, treat with amphotericin B in the first trimester and azoles in the second and third. Immunocompetent?

No antifungal therapy required. Conduct reassessment at 1-month to 3-month intervals for at least 1 year. Begin treatment with oral azole if pulmonary disease progresses or disseminates, or if symptoms persist for more than 2 months.
Signs of dissemination to meninges or other soft tissue?
Histologic examination and culture of suspicious skin lesions, analysis of joint effusion aspirates or lumbar puncture. Result?
Treat with oral azole. Amphotericin B for patients who do not respond to treatment with oral azoles or who have lesions in vital locations.
Treat with oral azole for 3-6 months.
